questions.concept: PEEK result after enqueue and dequeue sequence
questions.question: Starting with an empty queue: ENQUEUE(z), ENQUEUE(x), ENQUEUE(c), DEQUEUE(), ENQUEUE(v), DEQUEUE(). What does PEEK return now?
questions.explanation: Queue becomes z x c; DEQUEUE removes z; adding v gives x c v; DEQUEUE removes x, leaving c v, so PEEK returns c without deleting it.

questions.question: CFAA stands for:
questions.explanation: CFAA stands for the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

questions.question: What is the output of print('banana'.count('an'))?
questions.explanation: 'an' appears at index 1 and index 3 of 'banana', so count() returns 2.

questions.question: On a public network, an attacker uses a sniffer to capture all packets being exchanged. Which measure is suggested as protection against this sniffing?
questions.explanation: Sniffing captures all packets on a network, and a VPN is listed as the protection because it secures the traffic being captured.

questions.question: A field accepts ages from 18 to 60. A tester chooses the inputs 17, 18, 60 and 61. Which testing technique is being applied?
questions.explanation: Boundary value testing checks behaviour at and around the boundary values of a range, here just below, at, and just above 18 and 60.

questions.question: In paging, main (physical) memory is divided into fixed-size blocks called:
questions.explanation: Logical memory is divided into pages and physical memory into frames of the same size.

questions.concept: Noam Chomsky described as a linguist
questions.question: The hierarchy that organizes grammars and languages into four classes is credited to a person described as a linguist and computer scientist. Who is it?
questions.explanation: Noam Chomsky, a linguist and computer scientist, organized languages into the four-level Chomsky hierarchy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a concept similar to the Internet of Things?
questions.explanation: Web of Things, Cloud of Things and ubiquitous sensor networks are IoT-like concepts; 'virtual things' is not.

questions.question: Compared with secondary storage, primary storage is:
questions.explanation: Primary storage is faster but costs more per unit of storage than secondary storage.

questions.question: Which two OSI layers have no separate counterpart in the TCP/IP model, their functions being merged into the Application layer?
questions.explanation: TCP/IP lacks Session and Presentation layers; their functions are part of its Application layer.

questions.concept: Backup and recovery as DBMS advantage
questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of using a DBMS?
questions.explanation: DBMS advantages include backup and recovery, data sharing, security and reduced redundancy; isolation and dependence are file-system limitations.

questions.question: An Ethernet card (NIC) typically supports data transfer in which range?
questions.explanation: Ethernet cards support data transfer between 10 Mbps and 1 Gbps; 1-2 Mbps is the Bluetooth speed.

questions.concept: Degree of a tree from a given structure
questions.question: In a tree, root A has children B, C and D; B has children E and F; C has child G. What is the degree of the tree?
questions.explanation: Degree of a node is its number of children and degree of the tree is the maximum among all nodes. A has 3 children, which is the maximum.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Zigbee is INVALID?

options.A: Zigbee frequency range is mostly 2.4 GHz
options.B: Zigbee is a suitable communication standard for IoT

questions.explanation: Zigbee follows IEEE 802.15.4, mostly uses 2.4 GHz and suits IoT; the claim that its batteries are rechargeable is the invalid statement.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an e-governance model?
questions.explanation: E-governance covers models involving government (G2B, G2C, B2G, C2G); C2C is consumer-to-consumer trade with no government party.

questions.concept: Sum of range with start stop step
questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
total = 0
for i in range(2, 11, 3):
    total = total + i
print(total)
questions.explanation: range(2, 11, 3) produces 2, 5, 8 (11 is excluded), so the total is 15. Including 11 would wrongly give 26.

questions.question: As per the OOPS in C++ notes, how many pillars or concepts of OOPS are listed when classes and objects are included?
questions.explanation: The six listed concepts are classes, objects, abstraction, polymorphism, inheritance and encapsulation. Four is the count of core pillars without classes and objects.

questions.question: WordPress, Joomla and Drupal are examples of:
questions.explanation: WordPress, Joomla and Drupal are Content Management Systems used in web development.

questions.question: Which operating system is cited as an example of a client/server operating system?
questions.explanation: Windows 2000 is the client/server OS example. MS-DOS is a single-user single-tasking OS.

questions.concept: Prototyping and RAD suit full user involvement
questions.question: Users of a proposed system are willing to stay involved in every phase of the SDLC. Which process models are suitable choices in this situation? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: When users are involved in all phases of the SDLC, prototyping and RAD are the suitable choices. Waterfall limits user involvement after requirements, and Build and Fix is meant only for tiny programs.

questions.question: Which register holds the content of the memory word that has just been accessed?
questions.explanation: The MBR holds the data/content of the accessed memory word, while the MAR holds the address being accessed.

questions.concept: Exceptions handled at run time but errors not
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the difference between an error and an exception?

options.A: Exceptions can be handled at run time, but errors cannot
options.B: Errors can be handled at run time, but exceptions cannot
options.C: Neither can be handled once the program starts
options.D: Both are identical and handled the same way

questions.explanation: Exceptions are run-time problems that a program can catch and handle (for example with try-catch), whereas errors cannot be handled at run time.

questions.concept: append() adds a list as a single element
questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
lst = [1, 2]
lst.append([3, 4])
print(len(lst))
questions.explanation: append() adds its argument as one element, so the nested list [3, 4] becomes the third element. extend() would add each element separately.

questions.question: A guardian's phone number is changed in the STUDENT file but the old number remains in the ATTENDANCE file. Which limitation of a file system does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Data inconsistency occurs when the same data is maintained differently in different files, as happens when one copy is updated and another is not.

questions.question: An abstract machine studied in Theory of Computation is called:
questions.explanation: Automata is the study of abstract machines, and an abstract machine itself is called an automaton.
